html:
The Mixe, who call themselves Ayuukjä'äy, are an Indigenous people of the north-eastern highlands of Oaxaca, Mexico, around the peak of Zempoaltépetl. Their language belongs to the Mixe-Zoque family, related to Zoque and perhaps to the language of the Olmec.

Their rugged mountains kept them free of the Aztecs, and they long resisted the Spanish, rising again in the 1570s. They take pride in never having been fully conquered. Town assemblies and a system of rotating community offices still govern many villages, and Mixe brass bands are famous across Oaxaca. Their neighbours to the west are the Zapotec.
